steps.description: Run the primary differential expression contrast treated vs control on the 12,000-gene RSEM matrix using DESeq2. steps.name: limma-voom confirmation with quality weights

steps.context: The purpose is robustness, not a second opinion to cherry-pick from. DESeq2 on rounded expected counts and limma-voom with quality weights make different distributional assumptions and handle the low-depth sample differently (rounding + NB dispersion vs precision weighting), so agreement between them is meaningful evidence and disagreement localizes the fragility.

constraints: Use the same rounded-integer count matrix and the same 12 samples as the T1S2 full run, so the only differences are the model and the weighting

steps.description: Cross-check the primary DESeq2 contrast with an orthogonal method on the same 12 samples. A 12,000-gene matrix is smaller than a full transcriptome, so gene-set coverage is partial — report the match rate rather than assuming full overlap
steps.context: Human colon bulk RNA-seq, treated vs control. The reference store holds MSigDB 2026.1 human hallmark sets and the human GO biological-process collection as symbol-keyed GMT files, matching the counts matrix's gene-symbol identifiers. If either collection is absent at run time, run the analysis on whichever human symbol-keyed pathway collection is available (the store also holds human WikiPathways and oncogenic signatures) and say which was used — the enrichment layer annotates the DE result and its loss would not invalidate the primary answer.
steps.question: Which biological processes and hallmark programs are coordinately shifted in treated versus control colon samples?
constraints: Use human gene sets only — the data is Homo sapiens, colon; a mouse or rat collection would yield confident nonsense
Rank on the full DE result, not on a filtered significant subset
Use all genes that survived DE filtering as the ORA background, never the whole genome or the whole GMT universe
Set and report the fgsea random seed so the permutation p-values are reproducible

steps.description: Take the full ranked gene list from the T1S2 primary DESeq2 contrast — ranked by the shrunken log2 fold change or by sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue), stated explicitly — and run pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea) against human gene-set collections resolved from the environment's reference store: the human hallmark collection and the GO biological-process collection, both of which are keyed by HGNC gene symbols and therefore join directly to this matrix's gene-symbol row names with no ID conversion. Results tables with NES, nominal p, BH-adjusted p, set size and leading-edge genes are written for each collection
Redundant GO-BP sets are collapsed and both the raw and the collapsed count of significant sets are reported
A dot/bar plot of significant sets and enrichment curves for the leading hits are produced

Over-representation results for up- and down-regulated DE genes against the same collections are reported with all tested genes as background, or an explicit statement that too few genes passed FDR for ORA to be meaningful
The gene-symbol match rate between the counts matrix and each gene-set collection is reported

plan.title: Treated vs control colon RSEM DE + QC
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single RSEM gene-level expected-count matrix (12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples) plus a 12-row metadata table with one condition column: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. Two facts from the profile drive the design. First, RSEM expected counts are non-integer and the per-sample genes.results files carrying effective lengths were NOT delivered, so the tximport 'lengthScaledTPM'/average-transcript-length offset route is unavailable — the defensible fallback is to round expected counts to integers and run a standard negative-binomial DE, documenting that no length offset could be applied and that the resulting fold changes are therefore not corrected for treatment-driven isoform-length shifts. (tximport is not installed in this sandbox in any case; DESeq2, edgeR and limma are.) Second, sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which is a QC decision, not a cosmetic one: at n=6 per arm dropping it costs real power, and keeping it risks one low-depth sample dominating dispersion and clustering. T1S1 therefore quantifies the depth and outlier question explicitly (library sizes, detected-gene counts, PCA, sample-sample correlation, RLE) and returns a documented keep/drop recommendation rather than assuming one. T1S2 runs the primary DESeq2 contrast treated vs control on all 12 samples, and — regardless of the T1S1 recommendation — repeats the identical model with sample_01 excluded as a sensitivity analysis, reporting the overlap of the two hit lists so the reader can see how much of the answer rests on the shallow sample. T1S3 cross-checks the primary contrast with limma-voom (with quality weights, which explicitly down-weights a low-depth sample instead of removing it) to confirm the hits are not an artefact of one distributional assumption. T2S1 then takes the ranked DESeq2 statistic into GSEA against the staged human hallmark and GO-BP gene sets, which are present under /mnt/refs for Homo sapiens with HGNC symbols — matching the matrix's gene-symbol row names directly, no ID mapping needed. The 12,000-row matrix is small, so all steps are minutes of compute at modest memory.
